segments.title: Opening: address, date and introductions of the Pierce family
segments.summary: Allen records at the Pensacola home on 6 May 1961 and gets names, ages and instruments of those present, including Ida's sister Billie, De De Pierce and the children.

segments.title: Ida's birth year and a first round of songs and spirituals
segments.summary: Ida gives her birth year (1909) and Allen sets up the microphone; Ida, Sammy Lee and others sing and play spirituals and popular songs, with a break when Ida feels ill.

segments.title: Birthplace on Tarragona Street and a musical family
segments.summary: Ida was born in Pensacola on Tarragona Street; her mother and father came from Florida towns and both played piano, as do her sisters.

segments.title: Learning piano by gift and teaching the children
segments.summary: Ida says she never took lessons and has brought up her children in music, with Royce starting clarinet.

segments.title: Parents' church music, her mother's Georgia roots and Allen's own link
segments.summary: Her parents played church music, not jazz; Ida recalls her mother's schooling and Georgia birth, and Allen shares his own childhood in the same region.

segments.title: First bands: R.D. Jordan, Wally Mercy, Carl Davis, Harold Andrews and Charlie Broodin
segments.summary: Ida names the Pensacola bands she worked in, starting with R.D. Jordan, then they talk about saxophonist Charlie Broodin.

segments.title: The first jazz band she heard: Mack's band from New Orleans
segments.summary: Ida says the first jazz band she heard was a New Orleans band led by Thomas Mack, and that she later worked with him.

segments.title: Morris Park and New Orleans visitors: Edmund Hall, Buddy Petit, Lee Collins
segments.summary: Allen asks about Morris Park and New Orleans musicians who played there, such as Edmund Hall, Buddy Petit and Lee Collins.

segments.title: Who played in Mack's band and why New Orleans players stayed
segments.summary: Ida lists members of Mack's large band and explains that visiting bands got stuck in Pensacola and settled there.

segments.title: Edmund Washington and Ida's sister subbing in his group
segments.summary: Allen asks about saxophonist Edmund Washington; Ida describes him and says her sister played with him and she once filled in.

segments.title: Pianists Helen Jackson and Nellie Reese
segments.summary: Ida describes local women pianists Helen Jackson and Nellie Reese, and notes R.D. played drums.

segments.title: Personnel of R.D.'s first band and Alphonse Gambler
segments.summary: The first band had about six players including Charlie Bruden; Ida remembers trumpeter Alphonse Gambler.

segments.title: Pensacola style versus New Orleans style and band arrangement
segments.summary: Ida says early bands played by ear, did not have the New Orleans Dixie swing, and describes instrumentation and how solos were backed.

segments.title: Pensacola versus New Orleans on a new reel; the Goodson Swing
segments.summary: Asked again to explain the difference, Ida calls Pensacola music more swing and jazz than Dixieland, and plays a piece called the Goodson Swing.

segments.title: Tape experiments, songs, and Sammy Lee singing
segments.summary: Allen sets up the microphone again and Ida, her son and Royce perform songs while the freight train passes.

segments.title: New Orleans bands heard in Pensacola and Danny Barker
segments.summary: Ida heard Celestin and Louis Armstrong and remembers Danny Barker, whom Allen says is writing a play.

segments.title: Singing, advice for the young musicians, and changing the reel
segments.summary: Ida sings, offers advice to the girls, and Allen says the reel is about to run out.

segments.title: Songs on the new reel, taxi dance, and Sammy Lee playing
segments.summary: Ida and Sammy Lee sing and play several songs, and Ida mentions taxi dances where the band never stops.

segments.title: Spiritual singing, and Ida recaps her bands: R.D., Mack, Andrews and Wally Mercy
segments.summary: After more singing, Allen asks Ida to repeat her band history; she recounts R.D.'s band, Mack's, Andrews and 14-16 years with Wally Mercy around Pensacola clubs.

segments.title: Final performances and goodbyes
segments.summary: Sammy Lee and others sing Sweet Chariot, people joke, and the recording is wrapped up.
